questions.question: The Kd of the following proteins are given below: Protein A = 2, Protein X = 6, Protein Z = 9, Protein Y = 4. If the mixture of these proteins will be loaded onto a chromatography column, the protein eluting at last will be
The increase in height of distribution plane (H) will result in which of the following results?

answers.a: Increase in resolution of the column
answers.b: Decrease in resolution of the column
answers.c: Resolution depends on the height of the column and thus no change is observed
answers.d: Increase in number of distribution planes (N)

questions.question: Sodium azide is used in column chromatography as it helps to

answers.a: Prevent microbial growth while storing the column.

questions.question: The chromatographic technique used to separate analytes based on their size is

A gel filtration column was equilibrated with 50 mM Tris pH 7.5 containing 100 mM NaCl. The void volume of the column is 7 ml and the total volume is 25 ml. The column was calibrated with proteins A (10 kDa, Kd 0.44), B (30 kDa, Kd 0.38), C (50 kDa, Kd 0.33) and D (70 kDa, Kd 0.27). The unknown protein 'X' in the same column eluted at 12.56 ml. Based on the given data, the molecular weight (in kDa) of unknown protein 'X' will be
Which of the following protein elutes first from a size exclusion column? (Consider all proteins are monomeric and in native folded state.)
During gel filtration chromatography, the analyte is completely in the pore of the column if ____________.
What is the oligomeric status of a protein if the molecular weight obtained from gel filtration chromatography is 100 kDa and that determined by SDS-PAGE is 50 kDa?
A protein has the molecular weight of 500 kDa. Which of the following gel filtration column will be an ideal choice for separating the protein from a mixture?
The partition coefficient, Kd, depends on

answers.a: Only physical properties of the molecule
answers.b: Only chemical properties of the molecule
answers.c: Both physical and chemical properties of the molecule
answers.d: Is independent of the physical and chemical properties of the molecule
